blocking_findings.summary: ASKFLOOR-1-T3a-AC1: SCHEMA. `permission_decision_memory` gains nullable text columns `outcome`, `scope`, `scope_key`, `acting_person_id`, `acting_person_label` (physical snake_case — the table's existing convention; the deviation from the constitution's camelCase rule is recorded as deliberate in the migration note and the architecture note) and a CHECK `permission_decision_memory_human_row_ck`: `kind <> 'human_decision' OR (outcome IS NOT NULL AND scope IS NOT NULL AND scope_key IS NOT NULL AND acting_person_id IS NOT NULL)` (the label may be NULL — rows render "someone", 0154). The unconditional `permission_decision_memory_lookup_uq` is DROPPED and replaced by two partial unique indexes: `permission_decision_memory_lookup_uq` on `(app_id, agent_folder, kind, lookup_identity) WHERE kind <> 'human_decision'` and `permission_decision_memory_human_uq` on `(app_id, agent_folder, acting_person_id, scope, scope_key) WHERE kind = 'human_decision' AND revoked_at IS NULL`; the active lookup index stays. The migration is GENERATED (`npm run db:migrations:generate`, timestamp-named like `20260827174119_agents_web_ui_foundation.sql` — the currently live convention in `schema/migrations/`, not the retired `0107_`/`0110_` sequence) so the drizzle drift gate (`db:migrations:check`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml:63`) stays clean; the `meta/_journal.json` and snapshot travel with it. Human `id`s are UUID strings in the existing text column (no column type change). Tests (Postgres, `permission-decision-memory.postgres.integration.test.ts`, `schemaPrefix: 'permission_decision_memory'`): raw inserts prove (a) two non-human rows on the same four-column key still reject — the existing pin at `:154-175` is kept with its kind; (b) two ACTIVE human rows for the same person + scope + scope_key reject; (c) the same person + scope + scope_key with the first row REVOKED accepts a second row; (d) two different persons with the same scope + scope_key both insert; (e) a `human_decision` row missing any of outcome, scope, scope_key or acting_person_id rejects (one case each), and a missing label is accepted.

ASKFLOOR-1-T3a-AC2: PORT + REPOSITORY. `PermissionDecisionMemoryKind` gains `'human_decision'`; the row and put types gain optional `outcome?: HumanDecisionOutcome` (`allow | deny`), `scope?: HumanDecisionScope` (`exact | kind | place`), `scopeKey?`, `actingPersonId?`, `actingPersonLabel?` (closed typed enums exported from the port; no string literals elsewhere). The legacy methods `put`, `get`, `list` and `revoke` are for the non-human kinds only: each REFUSES `kind: 'human_decision'` (throws `HumanDecisionRequiresTypedAccessError`, a named domain error in the port — the human path has its own person-scoped methods below), `put` keeps today's conflict target, and an unfiltered legacy `list` (no `kind`) EXCLUDES human rows (`kind <> 'human_decision'`), so no legacy path can read or revoke across persons (0154/0118). NEW `putHumanDecision(input) → Promise<{ id: string; status: 'inserted' | 'refreshed' }>`: requires all four human fields and a v4-UUID-shaped `id` (a missing field or a malformed id throws before any SQL — the same guard style as `assertPersistable`, `:17-34`), always `lookupIdentity = scopeKey`, `decision = outcome`, `principal = canonicalTool`; it runs in ONE transaction: select the ACTIVE row for `(app_id, agent_folder, acting_person_id, scope, scope_key)` (the human partial index's key) — if one exists it is REFRESHED in place with `outcome`, `decision`, `reason`, `acting_person_label`, `effect_hash`, `rail_version`, `effect_schema_version`, `created_at` AND `provenance` re-encoded (AC5) with the STORED id, and the STORED id is returned with `status: 'refreshed'` (the caller's fresh id is discarded — an opposite-outcome write for the same authority simply replaces the older decision: newest human decision wins, one Forget still revokes the only active record, 0118); if none exists a NEW row is inserted with the caller's id and `provenance` encoded with it (`status: 'inserted'`) — a REVOKED row is NEVER reactivated: it stays as history beside the new row (the partial index ignores revoked rows, so the insert succeeds). NEW `listHumanDecisions({ appId, agentFolder, actingPersonId, includeRevoked? })` ordered newest first by `created_at`, person-scoped (no cross-person rows, pinned); `includeRevoked` defaults to false (active rows only); `true` returns revoked rows too, each with its `revokedAt` (pinned); NEW `revokeById({ appId, agentFolder, actingPersonId, recordId, nowIso })` → `'applied' | 'already_revoked' | 'not_found'` — `not_found` when the id exists for ANOTHER person, app or agent folder (never crosses any of the three axes, pinned by cross-person, cross-app and cross-folder tests); NEW `countExactAllowsByTool({ appId, agentFolder, actingPersonId })` → `Record<toolName, number>` of ACTIVE `outcome = allow`, `scope = exact` rows grouped by the canonical tool name carried in `principal` (the human row stores AC3's `canonicalTool` in the existing `principal` column — the trust-growth input read by T5a; documented in the architecture note). `getClassifierVerdict`/`putClassifierVerdict` are byte-identical. Tests: Postgres round-trips for each new method per person; unit guard test for the refusals.

ASKFLOOR-1-T3a-AC3: SCOPE KEYS in ONE module, NEW `application/permissions/human-decision-scope.ts`, ONE async function (async only because the native destination check awaits T2b's filesystem boundary; everything else is pure): `deriveHumanDecisionScopeKey({ outcome, scope, request, effectHash, workspaceRoot, canonicalRoot, trustGrowthTool }) → Promise<HumanDecisionScopeKeyResult>` where `HumanDecisionScopeKeyResult = { ok: true; scopeKey: string; pathOnly: boolean } | { ok: false; reason: HumanDecisionNotRememberableReason }` and `HumanDecisionNotRememberableReason` is the closed enum `protected_destination | no_category | no_root | incomplete_effect | deny_requires_exact` exported from this module (AC4 relays it verbatim, so no derivation logic is duplicated). Canonical tool identity: `canonicalTool = gantryNativeCanonicalToolName(request.toolName)?.canonical ?? request.toolName` (the helper returns `{ canonical, known } | null`, `application/permissions/gantry-tool-risk.ts:46`), so bare `file` and every registered `mcp__gantry__file` spelling are one tool, and the facade ids `WebSearch`/`WebRead` (`shared/gantry-tool-facades.ts:5-6`; `WebFetch` is already mapped to `WebRead` by the facade table) are used as given. Rules. `scope = exact`: `outcome = deny` ⇒ the full effect hash (`computePermissionEffectHash`, `domain/permission-effect-key.ts:48-99`, content included; `pathOnly: false`); `outcome = allow` on a NATIVE write (`FileWrite`/`FileEdit`): FIRST every supplied non-blank string destination among `file_path` and `path` is checked with `evaluateProspectiveWriteBoundary({ workspaceRoot, candidatePath })` (`shared/permission-prospective-write.ts`); any `inside: false` (outside, protected, hidden, secret, symlinked, undefined root) ⇒ `{ ok: false, reason: 'protected_destination' }` — protected destinations never key an Allow, whatever the destination count; then EXACTLY ONE destination ⇒ `exact:path:<canonicalTool>:<canonicalPath>` (`pathOnly: true`) using the `canonicalPath` the boundary now returns on success (T3a extends the shared helper's success result to `{ inside: true; canonicalPath: string }` — the resolved absolute path it already computes — because `application` may not import `node:path`, `scripts/architecture-map.json:84`); an all-safe dual input ⇒ the full hash (`pathOnly: false`); no string destination ⇒ full hash. `outcome = allow` on a VIRTUAL write — canonical `file` with `action: 'write'` → `(scope, path)` or `action: 'promote_scratch'` → `(targetScope, targetPath)` — ⇒ `exact:path:<canonicalTool>:<destination>` (`pathOnly: true`) when unprotected; every other allow ⇒ the full hash (`pathOnly: false`), so shell commands (redirects, `cp`, `mv`, `tee`, multi-target) are never path-only. The same request with `outcome = deny` always keys on the full hash (no destination check). virtual → `<normalizeFileArtifactScope(scope)>/<normalizeFileArtifactPath(path)>` (`domain/file-artifacts/virtual-path.ts`; an omitted `scope`/`targetScope` takes the same host default the normaliser applies) unless `isProtectedArtifactEntry` (`domain/file-artifacts/protected-virtual-path.ts`) or `protected: true` ⇒ `protected_destination` for an allow; a malformed shape (missing path, non-string fields, a normaliser throw) ⇒ full hash. `scope = kind` ⇒ `kind:<categoryId>` from this CLOSED request-to-category table (anything not in it ⇒ `{ ok: false, reason: 'no_category' }`): (1) `Bash`/`RunCommand`: parse with `parseBashCommand` (the same parser the read-only gate uses, `shared/auto-permission-read-only-gate.ts:93`), classify EVERY leaf with `classifyPermissionEffectShape(leaf, { stdinOk })` where `stdinOk` mirrors the gate EXACTLY: `false` for a single leaf, `true` for every leaf of any multi-leaf compound (`&&`, `||`, `;`, `|` alike — the parser exposes only aggregate topology, `:98-106`; pinned by a compound/pipeline parity test); all leaves `read_only_command` ⇒ `read_only_command`; all leaves `file_read` ⇒ `file_read`; a mix of those two ⇒ `read_only_command`; any `not_read_only` leaf, a parse failure or zero leaves ⇒ `no_category`; (2) canonical `file` with `action: 'list' | 'read'` ⇒ `virtual_file_read`; (3) `WebSearch` ⇒ `web_search`, `WebRead` ⇒ `web_read`; (4) trust growth (0154): `trustGrowthTool: true` ⇒ `kind:tool:<canonicalTool>` for ANY tool, evaluated before rows 1-3 (the card offers it only for high-risk gantry tools; T3a does not police that). The category ids are a closed exported enum `HumanDecisionKindCategory`. `scope = place` ⇒ `place:<canonicalRoot>` from the caller-supplied `canonicalRoot` (resolved by T3b via `resolveTrustedRootStage`; T3a only formats it) ⇒ `no_root` when absent or blank. `outcome = deny` with `scope ≠ exact` ⇒ `deny_requires_exact` (a No is always exact, 0154). An undefined `effectHash` (incomplete input) ⇒ `incomplete_effect` wherever the hash is needed (every deny; every non-path-only allow). Tests (unit, exhaustive): each shape × outcome × scope, dual native keys, bare `file` vs `mcp__gantry__file`, omitted virtual scope, protected/outside/symlink destinations, changed-content near-miss (same path, different content: allow keys equal, deny keys differ), whitespace-padded virtual paths, every kind row incl. multi-leaf pipelines and a mixed read/write pipeline ⇒ `no_category`, missing hash, missing root, deny with kind/place.

ASKFLOOR-1-T3a-AC4: SERVICE. NEW `application/permissions/human-decision-memory-service.ts` exporting `HumanDecisionMemoryService` (class, constructor-injected `{ repository, newId = randomUUID, now = currentIso }` — the `CapabilitySecretService` pattern, `application/capability-secrets/capability-secret-service.ts:17`; no adapter construction, port import only per `scripts/architecture-map.json`): `remember(dto: HumanDecisionRememberRequest) → { status: 'remembered'; id; shortId; scopeKey; pathOnly; stored: 'inserted' | 'refreshed' } | { status: 'not_rememberable'; reason: HumanDecisionServiceRefusal }` where `HumanDecisionServiceRefusal = HumanDecisionNotRememberableReason | 'unresolved_person' | 'once_never_remembered'` — refuses a blank `actingPersonId` (`unresolved_person`) and a `resolution` whose `kind` is not `'remember'` (`once_never_remembered`: a scalar `allow_once`/`allow_persistent_rule`/`cancel` never reaches the store) BEFORE any repository call; derives the key via AC3 and relays an `ok: false` reason verbatim; generates a v4 UUID via `newId` and validates its shape (a malformed injected id ⇒ throws — pinned); writes via `putHumanDecision` with `reason` = the DTO's human-readable line, `railVersion`/`effectSchemaVersion` from the DTO (the caller's rails catalogue), `principal = canonicalTool`; the returned `id` is the repository's EFFECTIVE stored id (a refreshed duplicate returns the stored id, never the discarded fresh one — pinned) and `shortId` is derived from it. `deriveHumanDecisionShortId(id, siblings: string[])` (exported, tested): the first 6 hex characters of the dash-free lowercase UUID, extended one character at a time only while another id in `siblings` (this person's ACTIVE records) shares the prefix — so short ids are unique within a person's active list; `list({ appId, agentFolder, actingPersonId, limit? })` → active rows newest first; short ids are disambiguated against ALL of the person's active ids BEFORE `limit` is applied, so a truncated page never shows an ambiguous short id (pinned); `revoke({ appId, agentFolder, actingPersonId, recordId })` → the repository's result verbatim (the full record id; prefix resolution is T5b's); `countExactAllowsByTool(...)` → the repository's map. Tests (unit, in-memory fake repository): every refusal reason, once-never-remembered for each scalar mode, malformed injected id, a remembered allow and deny round-trip, refreshed duplicate returns the stored id, list is person-scoped, short-id derivation incl. a 6-char collision extending to 7, revoke results.

ASKFLOOR-1-T3a-AC5: DOMAIN TYPES (T3b/T3c only consume them; all additive). `domain/types.ts` sits exactly at its 740-line architecture ceiling (`scripts/architecture-map.json:41`), so the ONLY change there is `PermissionDecisionSource` gaining `'human_decision'` on its existing `prettier-ignore` union line (`:257-260`, no new line); every other addition lives in the NEW sibling module `domain/human-decision.ts` (imported by the port, the scope module, the service and T3b/T3c; `types.ts` does not re-export it): the structured, provider-neutral remember resolution beside today's scalar modes — `HumanDecisionOutcome`/`HumanDecisionScope` re-exported here from the port for callers, `PermissionRememberResolution = { kind: 'remember'; outcome: HumanDecisionOutcome; scope: HumanDecisionScope }`, `PermissionApprovalResolution = { kind: 'mode'; mode: PermissionApprovalDecisionMode } | PermissionRememberResolution` (the option/claim DTO the story plan names; T3c owns wiring it into `PermissionCallbackClaimIntent`, the recovery envelope, settlement and the provider codecs — T3a only defines the type and its two guards `isRememberResolution`/`resolutionMode`); NEW `HumanDecisionRememberRequest` DTO = `{ appId, agentFolder, actingPersonId, actingPersonLabel?, resolution: PermissionApprovalResolution, request: PermissionApprovalRequest, effectHash?, workspaceRoot?, canonicalRoot?, trustGrowthTool?, railVersion, effectSchemaVersion, reason }`; NEW provenance codec `encodeHumanDecisionProvenance({ id, actingPersonId, outcome, scope, railVersion }) → string` / `decodeHumanDecisionProvenance(text) → {…} | undefined` (a fixed `human_decision:` prefix with a canonical sorted-key JSON body; decode fails closed on any other prefix, a malformed body, a missing field, a non-integer `railVersion` or a non-UUID id) — the `provenance` column of a human row is always the encoded form and never free text (the agent-visible provenance per 0054/0107 is derived from it, never inferred from strings). Tests: codec round-trip incl. `railVersion`, fail-closed decode for each malformed case, the resolution guards.

ASKFLOOR-1-T3a-AC6: architecture note `docs/architecture/permission-decision-memory.md` (or the existing decision-memory note if one exists — the implementer checks and extends rather than duplicates) records the record kind, the per-kind keys, the `principal = canonicalTool` convention for human rows, the snake_case physical names and the history-not-reactivation rule; existing unit and Postgres integration suites pass; tsc and check:architecture green; the drizzle drift gate clean (AF-AC7). GATE ENVIRONMENT: `stage done` runs every `verify_commands` entry in ONE environment with `GANTRY_TEST_DATABASE_URL` exported (the Postgres lane refuses without it), and today `verify.py`'s `npm test` general integration lane (`vitest.integration.config.ts`, file-parallel) then fails on `Hook timed out in 10000ms` in `beforeAll` for the DB-gated suites (concurrent schema migrations against one database — eleven suites, each green alone). T3a therefore sets `fileParallelism: false` in `vitest.integration.config.ts` ONLY when `GANTRY_TEST_DATABASE_URL` is set (URL-less runs keep today's parallelism; the Postgres config already runs serially), so `verify.py` passes with the URL exported and the gate is honest end to end.
